question_text: Explain in brief structure of Insulin.

steps.label: What insulin is
steps.why: Insulin is a protein, which is why it has to be injected rather than swallowed: the gut would digest it.
common_mistakes: Calling insulin a steroid hormone. It is a protein hormone.
Naming the wrong cells. Beta cells make it.
steps.memory_tip: Beta cells of the pancreas make insulin.
steps.margin_note: Name the hormone type and the cells.
lines: Insulin is a protein hormone secreted by
the β cells of the pancreas.

steps.label: The two chains
steps.why: The two chains are made as one piece and only later cut apart, which is why their lengths add up to less than the original.
common_mistakes: Giving one chain. There are two.
Swapping the chain lengths. A is 21, B is 30.
steps.margin_note: Write the numbers on their own line.

steps.label: The disulphide linkages
steps.why: Without the sulphur bridges the two chains would simply drift apart and the hormone would not work.
common_mistakes: Naming hydrogen bonds. The chains are held by disulphide linkages.
steps.memory_tip: Sulphur bridges hold the two chains together.
steps.margin_note: One line, but it is a whole mark.

steps.label: Proinsulin and C peptide
steps.why: The extra stretch holds the chains in the right shape while the bridges form, and is cut out once they have.
common_mistakes: Saying insulin is made in its final form. It is made as proinsulin.
steps.memory_tip: Proinsulin loses the C peptide to become insulin.
steps.margin_note: End with the C peptide. It is the marked name.
